newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid to buy Thrifty Payless - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid to buy Thrifty Payless - WSJ.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp has agreed to buy Thrifty Payless Holdings Inc for nearly $1.4 billion in stock plus the assumption of debt, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
The newspaper quoted Rite Aid's chief executive officer, Martin Grass, as saying the company would pay 0.65 of its shares for each Thrifty share or about $23.30 a share in Rite Aid stock.
It said the company would also assume about $890 million in Thrifty debt.
The newspaper cited Grass as saying he expected the deal to add "a few pennies" to per-share earnings in the year after the closing, which is scheduled to occur at the beginning of next year.
Both companies are to announce the deal on Monday, it said, adding that it would create one of the largest drugstore chains in the United States.

Their shareholders have yet to vote on the acquisition but buyout firm Leonard Green & Partners and Kmart Corp -- which control more than 40 percent of Thrifty stock -- have already agreed to vote in favor of it, the newspaper said.
Rite Aid is also expected to announce on Monday that it will pull out of Alabama, Florida, Georgia, and North and South Carolina, which together have 300 drug stores, it added.
Rite Aid is based in Camp Hill, while Thrifty has its headquarters in Wilsonville, Ore.
